# Error codes (REL-002)

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_error_codes.py from kernel/cemkit/core/error.hpp. Do not edit. -->

Every failure is classified with exactly one of these codes. The list is append-only: a
code is never renamed, renumbered or reused, and new codes are added at the end. Stored
data and the JSON interface use the name; the integer is used only across the C ABI.
0 is never a valid code. JSON Schema: `schemas/cemkit/v1/error-codes.json`.

| Code | Name | Meaning |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | `spec_rejected` | The spec failed validation and was not compiled. |
| 2 | `infeasible_requirement` | The stated requirements cannot be met together, or not by the selected product family. |
| 3 | `out_of_validity` | A model was asked for a value outside its stated validity range; no number is returned. |
| 4 | `geometry_failed` | Geometry generation failed or produced an invalid solid. |
| 5 | `mesh_failed` | Meshing failed or the mesh did not pass its quality checks. |
| 6 | `sim_untrusted` | A simulation ran but its result did not pass the trust gate. |
| 7 | `resource_exceeded` | A job exceeded its memory, time or disk budget. |
| 8 | `invalid_input` | An argument was malformed or outside its domain (for example NaN, a negative uncertainty or a malformed version string). |
| 9 | `unknown_unit` | A unit in the input is not one the spec compiler recognises. |
| 10 | `unit_mismatch` | A value's unit has the wrong dimension for the field it was given for. |
| 11 | `internal_error` | A defect in cemkit itself; it should be reported and fixed. |
| 12 | `not_implemented` | The operation exists in the interface but this family or module does not provide it yet; no value is returned. |

## Simulation statuses (TRUST-004)

Simulation results carry their own status (a separate type, added in M3). A status that
ends a candidate is classified as follows; VERIFIED and CONVERGED are not failures.

| TRUST-004 status | Error code |
| --- | --- |
| SOLVER\_FAILED | `sim_untrusted` |
| UNCONVERGED | `sim_untrusted` |
| MESH\_INVALID | `mesh_failed` |
| RESOURCE\_LIMIT | `resource_exceeded` |

## What an error carries

- the code;
- a message;
- a subject: the spec field path or model parameter concerned (may be empty);
- details: key/value pairs sorted by key, conventionally `value`, `unit`, `bounds` and
  `model`.

Messages are deterministic: no memory addresses and no locale-dependent formatting.
Numbers are written in the shortest form that reads back to the same value.
